observation.visible_scene: A full-frame close-up of an iridescent thin-film surface (interference colors of a soap-film/oil-slick type), composed of vertically flowing streaks and swirling eddies in magenta, yellow, cyan, green and violet over a pale grey-mauve base. No discrete objects, edges or background are visible—only the continuously varying color field.
visible_changes: The vertical streak bands in the centre undulate and stretch slowly throughout the excerpt, with their cyan/yellow cores wavering side to side.

The prominent yellow-and-magenta swirl on the right side deforms: it elongates and its internal colour bands reorganise from a rounded hook (early frames) toward a more vertical, streaked shape (later frames).
The magenta/violet swirl in the upper-left broadens and shifts slightly rightward and downward relative to its first-frame position.
The lower-right region gains more green/cyan area over time, while the lower-left dark green band persists but its boundary wiggles.
Local hue shifts occur within fixed regions (e.g. yellow patches bleeding into pink/green) rather than whole bands translating rigidly.
The overall pattern shows no clear start or stop; the morphing is already in progress at t=0 and continues to the last frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: The physical cause of the flow (drainage, air current, hand motion, etc.) and the material identity of the film are not shown.
What preceded t=0 and what follows t=2.67 s is unknown; the segment is a temporal crop with arbitrary endpoints.
Whether the colour field is a soap film, oil slick, or other interference surface cannot be confirmed from the pixels alone.
uncertain_details: Because the entire frame is the moving pattern, a slight global drift of the colour field cannot be reliably separated into camera motion versus surface flow; the apparent slow rightward/upward creep of features may be either.
Exact direction and speed of individual eddies are hard to track as colours blend and re-form, so only net deformation is confidently stated.
No sharp editing cut is observed; changes appear continuous.
